Thought: The IR spectrum shows a strong absorption band at 1712 cm⁻¹, which is characteristic of a C=O (carbonyl) group. This wavenumber is typical for ketones or aldehydes. Since there is only one peak in the carbonyl region (around 1670-1820 cm⁻¹), the molecule contains exactly one C=O group.

To confirm this, I could also check the 13C NMR spectrum since carbonyl carbons typically appear around 170-220 ppm, but since the IR spectrum clearly shows one carbonyl absorption and no other peaks in the carbonyl region, I can confidently determine that there is one C=O group.
Final Answer: 1
